title.narrative: Strengthening Sub-National Public Sector Results-Based Management in Lagos, Nigeria

description.narrative: The objective of this grant is to strengthen the use of performance information to manage for development results in Lagos State. Lagos State Government has expressed a strong interest for support to improve results-based reporting in the public sector that will provide a practical platform for strategic planning, risk management, progress monitoring, and outcome evaluation. The State Planning Commissions have the legislative mandate to coordinate the institutionalization of a harmonized M&E framework at sub-national levels of government and that would provide a platform for tracking the progress of actors in improving the quality of life of citizens. In Lagos State, the Ministry of Economic Planning and Budget has the statutory responsibility of monitoring the implementation of development programs and projects. The Ministry has had challenges in carrying out this function due to weak capacity and a poor culture of accountability in the MDAs. Although the Ministry has established a department of Monitoring and Evaluation that has a Director and adequate staff, there are still significant weaknesses that need to be addressed in the M&E system. Monitoring has been the main focus of M&E activities, and does not link activities to development results such as the State Government#s ten-point agenda. There are no formal mechanisms for evaluating programs and public reporting of performance is largely limited to statistical and reports. However, the enactment of the Fiscal Responsibility Act, which stipulates that management of public resources must be fully transparent and accountable, has brought the need for results-based reporting to the fore. Therefore, this IDF grant will assist the State to strengthen the institutional M&E system to generate timely reports that capture key performance indicators.
